nodes.title: High availability: Key Ideas
nodes.content: HA means designing so a single failure doesn't take the service down. Build redundancy at every layer the SLA cares about — power, network, compute, storage, region. Measure with availability percentages (the 9s) and recovery objectives (RTO/RPO).

flashcards.front: Active-active vs active-passive — when do you use each?
flashcards.back: Active-active: both nodes serve traffic; failure of one cuts capacity in half but service continues — no failover delay. Active-passive: only primary serves traffic; secondary is hot standby, takes over on failure with seconds-to-minutes delay. Active-active is harder (concurrency, conflict resolution) but better RTO. Active-passive is simpler — pick it for stateful systems that can't easily multi-write (most RDBMS).

flashcards.front: RTO vs RPO — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: RTO (Recovery Time Objective): how long until the service is back. RPO (Recovery Point Objective): how much data you can afford to lose. An RTO of 4h + RPO of 15 min means 'we can be down 4 hours and lose up to the last 15 minutes of writes'. Drives architecture choices: tight RPO needs synchronous replication; loose RPO allows async backups.

flashcards.front: The 'nines' — what does 99.9% vs 99.99% mean in real time?
flashcards.back: 99% (two 9s): ~3.65 days/yr of downtime. 99.9% (three 9s): ~8.76 hours/yr. 99.99%: ~52 minutes/yr. 99.999% (five 9s): ~5 minutes/yr. Each 9 typically multiplies cost ~10x because you need geographic redundancy, faster failover, and a much smaller deploy blast radius. Don't promise more 9s than the business actually values.

flashcards.front: Why is testing failover the hardest part of HA?
flashcards.back: An HA setup that's never been tested isn't HA — it's hope. Real-world failure modes are messier than 'kill primary' tests: cert expiry, DNS TTLs, partial-write states, split brain, runbooks out of date. Chaos engineering (Netflix's Chaos Monkey, AWS Fault Injection Simulator) makes failure normal — small failures every week so the big one isn't novel.

pairs.stem: FortiGuard provides various subscription services. An administrator wants to enable URL category-based web filtering on a FortiGate. Which FortiGuard subscription must be active?
pairs.option: FortiGuard Web Filtering subscription,.

pairs.stem: An administrator needs to insert a FortiGate into an existing network between two switches without changing IP addressing on any device. The FortiGate should pass all traffic transparently and apply security policies. Which deployment mode achieves this?
pairs.option: Transparent mode — FortiGate operates as a Layer 2 bridge with no IP on physical interfaces.

pairs.stem: A security analyst notices that a FortiGate security policy is matching traffic but the actions from the attached IPS profile are not taking effect. What is the most likely cause?
pairs.option: The policy's inspection mode is set to flow-based, which does not support IPS profiles

pairs.stem: A FortiGate has two WAN interfaces: WAN1 (100 Mbps, primary ISP) and WAN2 (50 Mbps, backup ISP). The administrator wants traffic to use WAN1 unless it goes down, then automatically fail over to WAN2. What FortiGate feature achieves this?
pairs.option: Enable ECMP (Equal Cost Multi-Path) routing with both WAN interfaces at equal metric, distributing load across both ISPs

pairs.stem: An administrator must prevent all users on the internal network from accessing social media sites during business hours (08:00–17:00, Mon–Fri) but allow access outside these hours. What combination of FortiGate features achieves this?
pairs.option: Create an application control profile blocking social media categories and attach it to a permanent security policy

pairs.stem: A FortiGate is configured with multiple security policies. Traffic from the LAN is being denied despite a policy that should allow it. What is the most likely reason?
pairs.option: The FortiGate evaluates security policies top-to-bottom and uses the first matching policy;.

nodes.title: Troubleshooting methodology: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A structured troubleshooting process beats random guessing every time. The classic flow: identify the problem precisely, form a theory, test it, fix, verify, document. Most exams test that you know the flow AND can spot the layer at which the symptom originates.

flashcards.back: CompTIA's 6-step: (1) Identify the problem (gather symptoms, questions to user, recent changes). (2) Establish a theory of probable cause. (3) Test the theory. (4) Plan and implement the fix. (5) Verify full system functionality, apply preventive measures. (6) Document everything.

flashcards.front: Top-down vs bottom-up troubleshooting on a network problem.
flashcards.back: Top-down: start at the application layer and work down — does the browser work? DNS? TCP? Routing? Bottom-up: start at the physical layer — is the cable plugged in? Link light? IP? When you suspect physical/cable, bottom-up is faster. When the user has 'a website is broken', top-down is faster.

Almost every production incident traces back to a recent change — a deploy, a config push, a vendor patch, a cert rotation. 'It was working yesterday' tells you to check today's change-log before forming an exotic theory. Recent changes are the highest-priors of the bug space.

Bisect the path between symptom and cause. If 10 hops between client and server, test hop 5. Good → problem is past hop 5. Bad → problem is before. Two more bisections narrow it to one hop. Faster than checking every link sequentially when the chain is long.

pairs.stem: A FortiGate administrator needs to collect and correlate logs from multiple FortiGate devices across several branch offices into a single management console for analysis and reporting. Which Fortinet product is designed for this purpose?
pairs.option: FortiAnalyzer, which collects logs.

pairs.stem: Remote workers need to access internal company resources using FortiGate SSL VPN. After connecting via the web portal, users can only access the resources listed in the portal bookmarks, not arbitrary internal IPs. What must be configured to allow full network access?
pairs.option: Configure the SSL VPN portal as a full-access tunnel portal with the 'Tunnel Mode' option enabled, and assign users an IP from a tunnel IP pool so the client gets a virtual adapter with LAN access

pairs.stem: An administrator needs to configure a site-to-site IPsec VPN between a FortiGate (HQ) and a branch office FortiGate. Both have static public IPs. The tunnel must use IKEv2 with pre-shared key authentication. Which Phase 1 settings are mandatory?
pairs.option: Remote gateway IP, digital certificate, and Diffie-Hellman group; certificates are required for IKEv2

pairs.stem: A FortiGate administrator needs to verify whether a specific IP address matches any firewall policy and which policy it would match. Which diagnostic tool is most effective for this?
pairs.option: Use the policy lookup tool in the FortiGate GUI: Policy & Objects > Policy Lookup.

pairs.stem: A user reports they cannot access a specific website. The FortiGate web filter log shows the site is blocked under the 'Unrated' category. The administrator verifies the site is legitimate. What is the quickest solution?
pairs.option: Submit the site to FortiGuard for re-categorization and wait for the rating database to update

pairs.stem: A FortiGate administrator needs to enable remote management access via HTTPS only on the WAN interface for a specific administrator's IP address (198.51.100.5). What two configurations are required?
pairs.option: Enable HTTPS on the WAN interface and configure an address object for 198.51.100.5 in the admin profile

pairs.stem: A FortiGate administrator wants to configure web filtering to allow access to the 'Video Streaming' category only for the marketing department users, while blocking it for all other users. What is the correct approach?
pairs.option: Create two security policies: one for marketing users (linked via FSSO group) with a permissive web filter profile.

pairs.stem: FortiGate has an IPsec VPN tunnel that has been working correctly. Users report they can no longer access resources across the tunnel. What is the first CLI diagnostic command the administrator should run to verify the tunnel status?
pairs.option: diagnose debug application ike -1 — enables verbose IKE debugging to trace tunnel negotiation in real time

pairs.stem: An administrator wants to implement network segmentation by creating multiple isolated networks on FortiGate. Each network segment should have its own policies and not share routing tables with others. Which FortiGate feature provides this logical separation?
pairs.option: Configure security zones with separate address objects and apply inter-zone policies to control traffic

pairs.stem: An administrator has configured a FortiGate policy with source address 'all' and destination address 'all' for internet access, with NAT enabled. A security audit flags this as overly permissive. Which addresses should replace 'all' for the source?
pairs.option: Replace with a subnet address object matching the specific LAN interface subnet only.

pairs.stem: A FortiGate is receiving IPsec VPN connections from remote FortiClients but some clients with dynamic IP addresses cannot establish the VPN. The Phase 1 is configured with the remote gateway set to a static IP. What change resolves this?
pairs.option: Change the remote gateway type in Phase 1 from 'Static IP Address' to 'Dialup User' to accept connections from any source IP

pairs.stem: A FortiGate web filter profile is configured to redirect blocked websites to a FortiGate-hosted 'Access Denied' page. Users report the block page is not appearing — instead they see a browser connection error. What is the most likely cause?
pairs.option: The block page only displays when the security policy uses proxy-based inspection mode; flow-based mode cannot deliver block pages

pairs.stem: An administrator configures email alerts on FortiGate for critical security events. After configuration, no emails are being received despite security events occurring. What should be verified first?
pairs.option: Verify the FortiGate can reach the SMTP relay server: check routing.

pairs.stem: An administrator is configuring explicit web proxy on FortiGate for users who have their browsers set to use a proxy server. Which FortiGate configuration is needed to enable explicit proxy?
pairs.option: Enable the explicit web proxy feature on the FortiGate interface where clients connect.

pairs.stem: An administrator needs to verify that a specific user (jsmith@company.com) was authenticated via FSSO and identify which FortiGate security policy is being applied to their traffic. Which CLI command provides this information?
pairs.option: get user fsso list — lists FSSO-connected users and their current session details

pairs.stem: An administrator must configure FortiGate to protect a web application from OWASP Top 10 attacks including SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF. Which FortiGate security profile provides web application-level protection?
pairs.option: Application Control profile with the 'Web Application' category set to monitor mode

pairs.stem: A FortiGate administrator wants to use FortiGate as a DNS server for the internal network and apply DNS filtering to block malicious domains. What configuration is required?
pairs.option: Configure FortiGate as a DNS server (System > DNS.

pairs.stem: A FortiGate security policy has 'log all sessions' enabled. The administrator notices the log storage fills up quickly. They only need to log denied traffic and allowed traffic to specific sensitive servers. What is the best configuration change?
pairs.option: Disable all logging and use SNMP traps to capture critical security events instead
